narrative.text:
ENCOUNTER:
On March 28, 2024, at approximately 0640 hours, Border Patrol Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] were conducting traffic observation on Interstate 94 near Jackson, Michigan, when the Michigan State Police requested assistance with a commercial vehicle inspection. Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] identified himself as a Border Patrol Agent to the vehicle's passenger, the subject, and questioned him as to his citizenship and immigration status.
IDENTITY AND STATUS:
The subject stated that he is a citizen and national of Honduras. He presented a Honduran passport issued in 2016 and a Honduran national identity card. He stated that he does not possess any visa, parole document or other document allowing him to enter or remain in the United States, and that he has never applied for any immigration benefit.
ENTRY:
The subject stated that on 09/15/2019 he crossed the Rio Grande on a raft near Roma, Texas, at approximately 2300 hours, together with eight other people, and walked inland without presenting himself for inspection at any port of entry. A smuggler arranged the crossing for a fee that his family paid.
TRAVEL:
He was driven from Roma to Houston, where he worked in construction until 2022, and then moved to Michigan by bus to work for a moving company.
IMMIGRATION AND CRIMINAL HISTORY:
Record checks returned no prior immigration encounters and no criminal history. The subject confirmed that he has never been arrested in the United States or in Honduras.
REMOVABILITY:
The subject is inadmissible under Section 212(a)(6)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, in that he is an alien present in the United States without being admitted or paroled. He was not admitted or paroled at any time after his entry.
DISPOSITION:
The subject was arrested, transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station, processed for a Warrant of Arrest and Notice to Appear (Form I-862), and released on an order of recognizance pending his hearing.
